def-discretization-invariant-operator-fa:
## Definition

Let $A$ and $U$ be spaces of functions on bounded domains $D$ and $D'$. A family of finite-dimensional maps $(G_n)_{n\ge1}$ is a **discretization-invariant approximation** of an operator $G:A\to U$ if each $G_n$ accepts input samples from a discretization of $D$, returns values that can be queried at arbitrary points of $D'$, and approximates $G$ as the input discretization is refined. In the compact-uniform version, for every compact $K\subset A$,
$$\sup_{a\in K}\|G_n(a)-G(a)\|_U\longrightarrow0.$$
The statement is about a single continuum operator and its compatible discrete realizations. It does not declare unrelated grid-specific maps to be one operator family.
def-physics-informed-neural-network-loss:
## Definition

Let $U\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain, let $\Gamma\subseteq\partial U$ be closed, let $L$ be a differential operator on $U$, and let $B$ be a boundary operator on $\Gamma$. Let $f:U\to\mathbb R$ and $g:\Gamma\to\mathbb R$ be target data. For a trial function $h$, define its residuals by $r_h(x)=L[h](x)-f(x)$ and $q_h(x)=B[h](x)-g(x)$. For $0<\alpha\le1$ and a function $v$ on a set $E$, define its Hölder seminorm by
$$[v]_{\alpha;E}=\sup_{x\ne y\in E}\frac{|v(x)-v(y)|}{|x-y|^\alpha}.$$
For positive fixed weights $\lambda_r,\lambda_b$, and probability measures $\mu_r$ on $U$, $\mu_b$ on $\Gamma$, the population loss is
$$\operatorname{Loss}^{\mathrm{PINN}}(h;\lambda)=\lambda_r\int_U|r_h|^2\,d\mu_r+\lambda_b\int_\Gamma|q_h|^2\,d\mu_b.$$
For residual collocation points $x_r^1,\ldots,x_r^{m_r}$ and boundary collocation points $x_b^1,\ldots,x_b^{m_b}$, the empirical loss is
$$\operatorname{Loss}^{\mathrm{PINN}}_{m}(h;\lambda)=\frac{\lambda_r}{m_r}\sum_{i=1}^{m_r}|r_h(x_r^i)|^2+\frac{\lambda_b}{m_b}\sum_{j=1}^{m_b}|q_h(x_b^j)|^2.$$
For $d\ge2$, its Hölder-regularized version is
$$\operatorname{Loss}_{m}(h;\lambda,\lambda_m^R)=\operatorname{Loss}^{\mathrm{PINN}}_m(h;\lambda)+\lambda^R_{r,m}[L[h]]_{\alpha;U}^{2}+\lambda^R_{b,m}[B[h]]_{\alpha;\Gamma}^{2}.$$
When $d=1$, all boundary points are available deterministically, no random boundary sample is used, and the source regularizes only the residual term. These are population and empirical functionals; they do not specify an optimization algorithm or assert that training reaches a global minimizer.
def-shin-elliptic-divergence-form-operat:
## Definition

Let $U\subset\mathbb R^d$ be open. For coefficients $a_{ij},b_i,c_i,d$ on $U$, define the positive divergence-form operator
$$L[u]=\sum_{i,j=1}^d D_i(a_{ij}D_j u)+\sum_{i=1}^dD_i(b_i u)+\sum_{i=1}^d c_iD_i u+du.$$
When the coefficients are continuously differentiable where needed, its nondivergence expansion is
$$L[u]=\sum_{i,j=1}^d a_{ij}D_iD_j u+\sum_{j=1}^d\widetilde b_jD_j u+\widetilde c\,u,$$
with
$$\widetilde b_j=\sum_{i=1}^dD_i a_{ij}+b_j+c_j,\qquad \widetilde c=\sum_{i=1}^dD_i b_i+d.$$
The **positive divergence convention** here means that the principal part is $+\sum_{i,j}D_i(a_{ij}D_j u)$. This sign is part of the definition.
def-shin-parabolic-operator-and-boundary:
## Definition

Let $U\subset\mathbb R^d$ be bounded, let $T>0$, and set $Q=U\times(0,T)$ and
$$\Gamma_T=(\bar U\times\{0\})\cup(\partial U\times[0,T]).$$
The final-time face $U\times\{T\}$ is excluded from $\Gamma_T$. For time-dependent coefficients define
$$L_t[u]=\sum_{i,j=1}^dD_i(a_{ij}(x,t)D_j u)+\sum_{i=1}^dD_i(b_i(x,t)u)+\sum_{i=1}^d c_i(x,t)D_i u+d(x,t)u.$$
Where the coefficient derivatives exist, write its nondivergence expansion as
$$L_t[u]=\sum_{i,j}a_{ij}D_iD_j u+\sum_i\widetilde b_iD_i u+\widetilde c\,u,$$
where $\widetilde b_i=\sum_jD_j a_{ji}+b_i+c_i$ and $\widetilde c=\sum_iD_i b_i+d$. For symmetric $a$, the drift also equals $\sum_jD_j a_{ij}+b_i+c_i$, the form used by the symmetric source consumers. The initial-boundary value problem uses the sign convention
$$-u_t+L_t[u]=f\quad\hbox{in }Q,\qquad u=\varphi\quad\hbox{on }\partial U\times[0,T],\qquad u=g\quad\hbox{on }\bar U\times\{0\},$$
with compatibility $g(x)=\varphi(x,0)$ on $\partial U$. Its residual for a trial function $h$ is $f+h_t-L_t[h]$, and its prescribed-data error is measured on $\Gamma_T$.

For the source notation $C_{2+\alpha}(Q)$, use the parabolic distance
$$d_p((x,t),(y,s))=(|x-y|^2+|t-s|)^{1/2}.$$
Let $B=U\times\{0\}$ and $S_\tau=\partial U\times[0,\tau]$. For $P=(x,\tau)\in Q$, set $\delta(P)=\inf_{R\in B\cup S_\tau}d_p(P,R)$ and $\delta_{P,Q}=\min\{\delta(P),\delta(Q)\}$. For an integer $m\ge0$, define
$$|v|_{m,\alpha}=\sup_{P\in Q}\delta(P)^m|v(P)|+\sup_{P\ne Q\in Q}\delta_{P,Q}^{m+\alpha}\frac{|v(P)-v(Q)|}{d_p(P,Q)^\alpha}.$$
The class $C_{2+\alpha}(Q)$ consists of functions for which
$$|u|_{0,\alpha}+\sum_i|D_i u|_{1,\alpha}+\sum_{i,j}|D_{ij}u|_{1,\alpha}+|u_t|_{2,\alpha}<\infty,$$
with the indicated derivatives continuous in $Q$. This fixes the source's weighted parabolic Hölder convention.
lem-pinn-random-samples-are-space-fillin:
## Statement

Let $d\ge1$, $s>0$, and let $X\subset\mathbb R^d$ carry a probability measure $\mu$. Fix an integer $m\ge1$ and $c>0$, and put $\varepsilon=(c\sqrt m)^{-1/s}$. Suppose there is a finite measurable partition $X_1,\ldots,X_K$ of $X$ at this particular scale such that each cell lies in a cube of side $\varepsilon$ and $\mu(X_j)\ge c\varepsilon^s$. Let $Y_1,\ldots,Y_m$ be independent random points each with law $\mu$. Then with probability at least
$$1-\sqrt m\left(1-\frac1{\sqrt m}\right)^m$$
every point of $X$ lies within Euclidean distance $\sqrt d\,c^{-1/s}m^{-1/(2s)}$ of at least one sample point. For an interior space of dimension $d$, use $s=d$; for a boundary space of Hausdorff dimension $d-1>0$, use $s=d-1$ and its own cell-mass constant. If $d=1$ and every boundary point is available deterministically, the boundary fill distance is zero and no random boundary sample is needed.
lem-shin-pinn-all-scale-cell-mass-assump:
## Statement

Let $X$ be a nonempty measurable space, let $d\ge1$, let $c>0$, and let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $X$. There is no family of finite measurable partitions $\mathcal P_\varepsilon$ of $X$, one for every $\varepsilon>0$, for which every cell $E\in\mathcal P_\varepsilon$ satisfies $\mu(E)\ge c\varepsilon^d$.
lem-shin-radial-smooth-cutoff:
## Statement

There exists $b\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)$ with $0\le b\le1$, $b(x)=1$ for $|x|\le1$, and $b(x)=0$ for $|x|\ge2$, such that the profile $\chi:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ defined by $\chi(r)=b(4r)$ is the restriction of a smooth function on $\mathbb R$, equals $1$ for $0\le r\le1/4$, and equals $0$ for $r\ge1/2$.

Here $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)$ denotes the infinitely differentiable, compactly supported real-valued functions.
lem-neural-operator-compact-union-under-:
## Statement

Let $(X,d_X)$ and $(Y,d_Y)$ be metric spaces, let $K\subseteq X$ be compact, and let $f,f_n:X\to Y$ be continuous for every integer $n\ge1$. Suppose that for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $N\ge1$ such that $d_Y(f_n(x),f(x))<\varepsilon$ for all $n\ge N$ and all $x\in K$.
Then
$$W=f[K]\cup\bigcup_{n=1}^{\infty}f_n[K]$$
is compact in $Y$. The empty-set case is included, and the proof uses no choice principle.
thm-neural-operator-input-output-spaces-:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain. Each of the real spaces $L^p(D)$ for $1\le p<\infty$, $W^{m,p}(D)$ for $m\in\mathbb N$ and $1\le p<\infty$, and $C^m(\bar D)$ for $m\in\mathbb N_0$ has the approximation property: on every norm-compact subset, the identity can be approximated uniformly by bounded finite-rank linear maps. Here the $C^m$ norm is the maximum of the uniform norms of the derivatives through order $m$, extended continuously to $\bar D$. The same conclusion holds for the output-space list with its dimension and regularity parameters.
alg-empirical-pinn-objective:
## Definition

Choose $0<\alpha\le1$ and positive residual and boundary weights $\lambda_r,\lambda_b$. For $d\ge2$, let $\mu_r$ and $\mu_b$ be the residual and boundary sampling measures. The constants $c_r,c_b>0$ satisfy $\mu_r(U_j^\varepsilon)\ge c_r\varepsilon^d$ and $\mu_b(\Gamma_j^\varepsilon)\ge c_b\varepsilon^{d-1}$ for the cells in the sample partitions at the selected small scales $0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_{0,r},\varepsilon_{0,b}$; $C_r,C_b>0$ satisfy $\mu_r(B_\varepsilon(x)\cap U)\le C_r\varepsilon^d$ and $\mu_b(B_\varepsilon(y)\cap\Gamma)\le C_b\varepsilon^{d-1}$. Require the upper ball-mass bounds at the selected fill radii, and take sample counts sufficiently large for both these radii and the partition scales to be in their specified ranges. Given sample counts $m_r,m_b$, put
$$\kappa_r=C_r/c_r,\qquad \kappa_b=C_b/c_b,$$
$$C_m=3\max\!\left\{\kappa_r(\sqrt d)^d m_r^{1/2},\ \kappa_b(\sqrt d)^{d-1}m_b^{1/2}\right\},$$
$$\widehat\lambda^R_{r,m}=\frac{3\lambda_r(\sqrt d)^{2\alpha}c_r^{-2\alpha/d}m_r^{-\alpha/d}}{C_m},\qquad \widehat\lambda^R_{b,m}=\frac{3\lambda_b(\sqrt d)^{2\alpha}c_b^{-2\alpha/(d-1)}m_b^{-\alpha/(d-1)}}{C_m}.$$
Choose regularization weights componentwise at least these thresholds and satisfying $\|\lambda_m^R\|_\infty=O(\|\widehat\lambda_m^R\|_\infty)$ as sample counts grow. Evaluate the Hölder-regularized objective from the preceding definition on a trial class. For $d=1$, set
$$C_m=3\kappa_r m_r^{1/2},\qquad \widehat\lambda^R_{r,m}=\frac{\lambda_r c_r^{-2\alpha}}{\kappa_r}m_r^{-\alpha-1/2},\qquad \widehat\lambda^R_{b,m}=0,$$
and use only the residual seminorm penalty. The thresholds are part of the source theorem and cannot be replaced by a generic positive penalty.
def-neural-operator-activation-classes:
## Definition

Fix an input dimension $q\ge1$ and an integer $m\ge0$. Let $\mathcal A_m^{(q)}$ be the class of continuous scalar activations $\sigma:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ for which there is one depth $n\in\mathbb N$ such that, for every compact $K\subset\mathbb R^q$, the scalar-output depth-$n$ multilayer perceptrons with activation $\sigma$ are dense in $C^m(K)$ in the $C^m$ norm. For vector outputs, stack scalar-output networks of that same depth. The source notation $\mathcal A_m$ suppresses the input dimension fixed by the finite-dimensional network under consideration. Let $\mathcal A_m^{L,(q)}$ be the subclass whose members are Borel measurable and have at most linear growth, meaning
$$\sup_{s\in\mathbb R}\frac{|\sigma(s)|}{1+|s|}<\infty.$$
For an integer $q\ge1$, define $\mathrm{BA}_q$ to consist of those $\sigma\in\mathcal A_0^{(q)}$ for which, for every compact $K\subset\mathbb R^q$, every $\varepsilon>0$, and every $C\ge\operatorname{diam}_2(K)$, there is a finite multilayer perceptron $f:\mathbb R^q\to\mathbb R^q$ with
$$|f(x)-x|_2\le\varepsilon\quad(x\in K),\qquad |f(x)|_2\le C\quad(x\in\mathbb R^q).$$
Here $\operatorname{diam}_2(K)=\sup_{x,y\in K}|x-y|_2$. The diameter-based global bound is part of this definition and is retained verbatim; its nonemptiness is checked separately.
lem-shin-elliptic-energy-estimate:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $U\subset\mathbb R^d$ be bounded Lipschitz. Let $A=(a_{ij})$ be a bounded measurable real symmetric matrix field, uniformly elliptic with eigenvalues at least $\lambda_0>0$, and let $b,c,d$ be bounded measurable real coefficient fields satisfying
$$\lambda_0^{-2}(\|b(x)\|^2+\|c(x)\|^2)+\lambda_0^{-1}|d(x)|\le v^2\qquad(x\in U).$$
For the divergence operator
$$L[e]=\sum_{i,j}D_i(a_{ij}D_j e)+\sum_iD_i(b_i e)+\sum_i c_iD_i e+de,$$
every real $e\in H^1_0(U)\cap C^2(U)\cap C^0(\bar U)$ with $L[e]\in L^2(U)$ satisfies
$$\|e\|_{H^1(U)}^2\le C_E\bigl(\|L[e]\|_{L^2(U)}^2+\|e\|_{L^2(U)}^2\bigr),$$
where $C_E$ depends only on $\lambda_0$ and $v$. The zero-trace condition is required for the integration by parts.
lem-shin-elliptic-residual-stability:
## Statement

Let $U\subset\mathbb R^d$ be bounded and open, and let
$$L[u]=\sum_{i,j=1}^d a_{ij}D_iD_j u+\sum_{j=1}^d\widetilde b_jD_j u+\widetilde c\,u$$
on $U$, where $a(x)$ is symmetric, $\xi^Ta(x)\xi\ge\lambda_0|\xi|^2$ for all $x\in U$ and $\xi\in\mathbb R^d$ with $\lambda_0>0$, the coefficients are continuous and bounded, and $\widetilde c\le0$. There is a constant $C_L<\infty$, depending only on $U$, $\lambda_0$, and the coefficient bounds, such that every $w\in C^2(U)\cap C^0(\bar U)$ with $L[w]\in C^0(U)$ satisfies
$$\|w\|_{C^0(U)}\le C_L\left(\|L[w]\|_{C^0(U)}+\|w\|_{C^0(\partial U)}\right).$$
In particular, for any two functions $u^*,h\in C^2(U)\cap C^0(\bar U)$,
$$\|u^*-h\|_{C^0(U)}\le C_L\left(\|L[u^*]-L[h]\|_{C^0(U)}+\|u^*-h\|_{C^0(\partial U)}\right).$$
lem-shin-bounded-open-set-hilbert-evolut:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $U\subset\mathbb R^d$ be bounded and open, $d\ge1$, and put $H=L^2(U;\mathbb R)$ and $V=H^1_0(U;\mathbb R)$, where the latter is the $H^1$-closure of $C_c^\infty(U)$. Then $V$ is a separable real Hilbert space, its inclusion into $H$ is continuous, injective and dense, and $(V,H,V^*)$ is a real evolution triple. The gradient norm and the full $H^1$ norm are equivalent on $V$. No regularity of $\partial U$ is required.
lem-shin-parabolic-energy-estimate:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $U\subset\mathbb R^d$ be bounded and open, $T>0$, $Q=U\times(0,T)$, and let
$$L_t[e]=\sum_{i,j=1}^dD_i(a_{ij}D_j e)+\sum_{i=1}^dD_i(b_i e)+\sum_i c_iD_i e+d e$$
with $a_{ij}=a_{ji}$, $a(x,t)\ge\lambda_0 I$ for some $\lambda_0>0$, and real measurable $a,b,c,d$ bounded with the spatial derivatives needed for the displayed divergence form. Let $V=H^1_0(U)$, $H=L^2(U)$, and let $e\in L^2(0,T;V)$ have weak derivative $e_t\in L^2(0,T;V^*)$ and satisfy $-e_t+L_t[e]=r\in L^2(U\times(0,T))$ weakly. Use its continuous $H$ representative for the initial datum $e(0)$ and endpoint norms. The source application has $e(0)=0$. Then there is $C_E<\infty$, depending only on $T$, $\lambda_0$, and the coefficient bounds, such that
$$\sup_{0\le t\le T}\|e(t)\|_{L^2(U)}^2+\int_0^T\|\nabla e(t)\|_{L^2(U)}^2\,dt\le C_E\left(\|e(0)\|_{L^2(U)}^2+\|r\|_{L^2(Q)}^2\right).$$
The spatial zero trace is the stated $V$ membership almost everywhere in time. In particular, the estimate applies to locally classical continuous errors once their energy-space membership and weak equation have been established; no closed-cylinder derivatives are required.
lem-shin-parabolic-residual-stability:
## Statement

Let $U\subset\mathbb R^d$ be bounded, $T>0$, and
$$P[w]=-w_t+\sum_{i,j=1}^d a_{ij}(x,t)D_iD_jw+\sum_{j=1}^d\widetilde b_j(x,t)D_jw+\widetilde c(x,t)w$$
on $Q=U\times(0,T)$. Suppose $a(x,t)$ is symmetric, $\xi^Ta(x,t)\xi\ge\lambda_0|\xi|^2$ with $\lambda_0>0$, $\widetilde b,\widetilde c$ are bounded and continuous, and $\widetilde c\le0$. There is $C_P<\infty$, depending only on $U,T,\lambda_0$ and the coefficient bounds, such that every $w\in C^{2,1}(Q)\cap C^0(\bar U\times[0,T])$ with $P[w]\in C^0(Q)$ satisfies
$$\|w\|_{C^0(Q)}\le C_P\left(\|P[w]\|_{C^0(Q)}+\|w\|_{C^0(\Gamma_T)}\right),$$
where $\Gamma_T=(\bar U\times\{0\})\cup(\partial U\times[0,T])$ excludes the final-time face.
alg-neural-operator-mesh-discretization:
## Definition

For the continuous-function architecture, given a finite partition of $D$ into measurable cells $E_1,\dots,E_N$, choose tags $\xi_j\in E_j$ and weights $\omega_j=|E_j|$. For input samples $v_0(\xi_j)$, replace each integral layer by
$$v_{t+1}^{(i)}=\sigma_t\!\left(W_tv_t^{(i)}+\sum_{j=1}^N\omega_j\kappa_t(\xi_i,\xi_j)v_t^{(j)}+b_t(\xi_i)\right),\qquad 1\le i\le N.$$
At an arbitrary output query $x\in\bar D'$, evaluate the same layer formula using $x$ in the first kernel argument and the stored input-cell values in the sum. Apply the pointwise lifting and projection networks with the same parameters at every discretization. A refinement changes the cells, tags, and weights, but not the continuum parameters $W_t,\kappa_t,b_t$ or the pointwise network parameters.
fs-shin-global-holder-dirichlet-claim:
## Statement

Let $0<\alpha<1$ and let $U\subset\mathbb R^d$ be bounded and satisfy an exterior sphere condition at every boundary point. Let $a_{ij}=a_{ji}\in C^{1,\alpha}(U)$ be uniformly elliptic with minimum eigenvalue at least $\lambda_0>0$, let $b_i\in C^{1,\alpha}(U)$ and $c_i,d\in C^\alpha(U)$, and define
$$L[u]=\sum_{i,j=1}^dD_i(a_{ij}D_j u+b_i u)+\sum_{i=1}^d c_iD_i u+du.$$
Assume $\sum_{i,j}|a_{ij}(x)|^2\le\Lambda$ and $\lambda_0^{-2}(\|b(x)\|^2+\|c(x)\|^2)+\lambda_0^{-1}|d(x)|\le v^2$ on $U$, and use the expanded coefficients $\widetilde b_j=\sum_iD_i a_{ij}+b_j+c_j$ and $\widetilde c=\sum_iD_i b_i+d\le0$. For every $f\in C^{0,\alpha}(U)$ and $g\in C^0(\partial U)$, the source assertion is that the Dirichlet problem $L[u]=f$ in $U$, $u=g$ on $\partial U$ has a unique solution $u\in C^{2,\alpha}(U)\cap C^0(\bar U)$. For any $h\in C^0(U)$ with $L[h]\in C^{0,\alpha}(U)$ and $h\in C^{0,\alpha}(\partial U)$, the source further asserts
$$\|u-h\|_{C^0(U)}\le C\bigl(\|f-L[h]\|_{C^0(U)}+\|g-h\|_{C^0(\partial U)}\bigr),$$
where $C$ depends only on the domain and the displayed coefficient bounds. The global existence part of this assertion is false under the library's bounded global Hölder convention.
def-fourier-neural-operator-layer:
## Definition

Let $\mathbb T^d=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^d$ with normalized Lebesgue measure, represented by the unit cube $[0,1]^d$, and let $v\in C(\mathbb T^d;\mathbb R^q)$ be a periodic vector field. Let $K\ge0$ be a frequency cutoff, and let $R_k\in\mathbb C^{q'\times q}$ be trainable matrices for integer multi-indices $k$ with $\|k\|_\infty\le K$. Define the truncated Fourier integral layer by
$$\mathcal K_Rv(x)=\sum_{\|k\|_\infty\le K}e^{2\pi i k\cdot x}R_k\widehat v(k),\qquad \widehat v(k)=\int_{\mathbb T^d}e^{-2\pi i k\cdot y}v(y)\,dy.$$
For real-valued outputs require $R_{-k}=\overline{R_k}$ and $R_0$ real. A Fourier neural-operator layer is
$$v_{t+1}(x)=\sigma\bigl(W_tv_t(x)+\mathcal K_Rv_t(x)+b_t(x)\bigr),$$
where $W_t$ is a real pointwise channel map, $b_t$ is a real bias function, and $\sigma$ acts coordinatewise. This definition gives a Fourier-parameterized layer only. It does not assert that the architecture is universal in any specified function-space topology.
lem-neural-operator-ba-class-is-empty-as:
## Statement

For each $q\ge1$, the class $\mathrm{BA}_q$ in the displayed activation-class definition is empty.
lem-neural-operator-kernel-riemann-sums-:
## Statement

Let $d,d'\in\mathbb N$ with $d,d'\ge1$, let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be nonempty, bounded, and Jordan measurable, let $D'\subset\mathbb R^{d'}$ be nonempty and bounded, let $\kappa\in C(\bar D'\times\bar D)$ be scalar-valued, and let $K\subset C(\bar D)$ be nonempty and compact in the supremum norm. Give products of metric spaces the max metric. Let $Q_n:C(\bar D)\to\mathbb R$ be bounded linear quadrature functionals with $\sup_n\|Q_n\|<\infty$ and $Q_n f\to\int_D f(y)\,dy$ for every $f\in C(\bar D)$. Then
$$\sup_{a\in K}\sup_{x\in\bar D'}\left|Q_n\bigl(\kappa(x,\cdot)a(\cdot)\bigr)-\int_D\kappa(x,y)a(y)\,dy\right|\longrightarrow0.$$
This conclusion is in the supremum norm on the output variable. It does not by itself establish convergence in an arbitrary Banach output norm $U$.
lem-pinn-residual-loss-from-fill-distanc:
## Statement

Let $d\ge2$, let $U\subset\mathbb R^d$ and $\Gamma\subset\mathbb R^d$ be measurable, and let $\mu_r$ and $\mu_b$ be probability measures on them. For positive integers $m_r,m_b$, let the residual samples $x_1^r,\ldots,x_{m_r}^r$ and boundary samples $x_1^b,\ldots,x_{m_b}^b$ form $\varepsilon_r$- and $\varepsilon_b$-nets of $U$ and $\Gamma$ in Euclidean distance. Assume that for every center $x\in U$ and $y\in\Gamma$,
$$\mu_r(\overline B_{\varepsilon_r}(x)\cap U)\le C_r\varepsilon_r^d,\qquad \mu_b(\overline B_{\varepsilon_b}(y)\cap\Gamma)\le C_b\varepsilon_b^{d-1}.$$
Suppose $[L[h]]_{\alpha;U}$, $[B[h]]_{\alpha;\Gamma}$, $[f]_{\alpha;U}$, and $[g]_{\alpha;\Gamma}$ are finite, where $[v]_{\alpha;E}=\sup_{x\ne y\in E}|v(x)-v(y)|/|x-y|^\alpha$. Let $\lambda_r,\lambda_b>0$, and use the population and empirical weighted-square PINN losses
$$\operatorname{Loss}^{\mathrm{PINN}}(h;\lambda)=\lambda_r\int_U|L[h]-f|^2\,d\mu_r+\lambda_b\int_\Gamma|B[h]-g|^2\,d\mu_b,$$
$$\operatorname{Loss}^{\mathrm{PINN}}_m(h;\lambda)=\frac{\lambda_r}{m_r}\sum_{i=1}^{m_r}|L[h](x_i^r)-f(x_i^r)|^2+\frac{\lambda_b}{m_b}\sum_{j=1}^{m_b}|B[h](x_j^b)-g(x_j^b)|^2.$$
Define
$$C_m=3\max\{C_rm_r\varepsilon_r^d,\ C_bm_b\varepsilon_b^{d-1}\},\quad \lambda^R_{r,m}=\frac{3\lambda_r\varepsilon_r^{2\alpha}}{C_m},\quad \lambda^R_{b,m}=\frac{3\lambda_b\varepsilon_b^{2\alpha}}{C_m}.$$
Then
$$\operatorname{Loss}^{\mathrm{PINN}}(h;\lambda)\le C_m\operatorname{Loss}^{\mathrm{PINN}}_m(h;\lambda)+C_m\left(\lambda^R_{r,m}[L[h]]_{\alpha;U}^2+\lambda^R_{b,m}[B[h]]_{\alpha;\Gamma}^2\right)+3\lambda_r\varepsilon_r^{2\alpha}[f]_{\alpha;U}^2+3\lambda_b\varepsilon_b^{2\alpha}[g]_{\alpha;\Gamma}^2.$$
lem-shin-interior-parabolic-schauder-est:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $0<\alpha<1$, and let $O\subset\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R$ be open. Use $\rho((x,t),(y,s))=\max\{|x-y|,\sqrt{|t-s|}\}$ and $[v]_{\alpha;E}=\sup_{z\ne z'\in E}|v(z)-v(z')|/\rho(z,z')^\alpha$. Suppose the symmetric matrix $A$, vector $\beta$ and scalar $q$ are locally $\alpha$-Hölder for this metric, and $\lambda I\le A\le\Lambda I$ with $0<\lambda\le\Lambda<\infty$. For every compact parabolic cylinder $K$ contained in the interior of a larger compact cylinder $K'\subset O$ there is $C<\infty$, depending on these cylinders, $d,\alpha,\lambda,\Lambda$ and the coefficient Hölder norms on $K'$, such that every smooth $u$ satisfying $u_t-A:D^2u-\beta\cdot Du-qu=F$ near $K'$ obeys
$$\|u\|_{C^{2+\alpha,1+\alpha/2}(K)}\le C\bigl(\|u\|_{L^\infty(K')}+\|F\|_{C^{\alpha,\alpha/2}(K')}\bigr).$$
Here the left norm consists of the suprema and parabolic $\alpha$-Hölder seminorms of $u,Du,D^2u,u_t$. The constant does not depend on derivatives of the coefficients above their displayed Hölder regularity. The assertion is an estimate for smooth solutions, not a prior assumption of classical solvability.
lem-shin-parabolic-classical-approximati:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice. Let $U\subset\mathbb R^d$ be nonempty, bounded and open, $T>0$, and $0<\alpha<1$. At every $x_0\in\partial U$ assume there is an exterior tangent closed ball, disjoint from $U$ and containing $x_0$ on its sphere. Let $A=A^T$, $\beta,q,f$ be bounded on $U\times(0,T]$, locally parabolic $\alpha$-Hölder up to its final face, with $\lambda I\le A\le\Lambda I$, $\lambda>0$, and $q\le0$. Let the combined initial and lateral datum $\psi$ be continuous on $\Gamma_T=(\bar U\times\{0\})\cup(\partial U\times[0,T])$, including compatibility at their intersection. Then there is a unique
$$u\in C^{2+\alpha,1+\alpha/2}_{\mathrm{loc}}(U\times(0,T])\cap C(\bar U\times[0,T])$$
with $-u_t+A:D^2u+\beta\cdot Du+qu=f$ and $u=\psi$ on $\Gamma_T$. It obeys $\|u\|_\infty\le\|\psi\|_\infty+T\|f\|_\infty$. Moreover it is the interior limit of smooth-coefficient weak solutions on finite polyhedral subdomains exhausting $U$, with uniform supremum bounds and the uniform compact-interior estimates just stated. If the coefficients possess a bounded divergence representation compatible in distributions, those approximants may be chosen by convolution of its original divergence coefficients.
lem-shin-zero-data-parabolic-classical-e:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice. Let $U\subset\mathbb R^d$ be bounded and open with an exterior tangent ball at every boundary point, and let $T>0$. Consider the intended divergence operator
$$L_tu=\sum_{i,j}D_i(a_{ij}D_ju)+\sum_iD_i(b_iu)+\sum_i c_iD_iu+du.$$
Assume $a=a^T\ge\lambda_0I$, $\lambda_0>0$, and $a,b,c,d$ bounded; the spatial derivatives of $a,b$ agree with distributional derivatives locally, and the expansion
$$\beta_j=\sum_iD_ia_{ij}+b_j+c_j,\qquad q=\sum_iD_ib_i+d$$
is locally valid with bounded $a,\beta,q$, locally parabolic $\alpha$-Hölder up to the final face, $0<\alpha<1$, and $q\le0$. Let $r$ be bounded and locally parabolic $\alpha$-Hölder up to that face. If $e$ is locally classical, bounded, continuous on the closed cylinder, zero on the initial and lateral faces, and satisfies $-e_t+L_te=r$, then
$$e\in L^2(0,T;H^1_0(U)),\qquad e_t\in L^2(0,T;H^{-1}(U)),\qquad e(0)=0\text{ in }L^2(U).$$
It is the unique zero-initial variational solution of that equation, and for a finite $C_E$ depending only on $T,\lambda_0$ and the divergence coefficient bounds,
$$\sup_{0\le t\le T}\|e(t)\|_2^2+\int_0^T\|De(t)\|_2^2dt\le C_E\|r\|_{L^2(U\times(0,T))}^2.$$
Consequently a sequence of such errors with $\|e_m\|_\infty\to0$ and $\|r_m\|_\infty\to0$ converges strongly to zero in $L^2(0,T;H^1(U))$. No closed-cylinder derivative regularity is assumed.
thm-shin-parabolic-initial-boundary-exis:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice. Let $U\subset\mathbb R^d$ be nonempty, bounded and open, $T>0$, $Q=U\times(0,T)$, and $0<\alpha<1$. Use the intended divergence operator
$$L_tu=\sum_{i,j}D_i(a_{ij}D_ju)+\sum_iD_i(b_iu)+\sum_i c_iD_iu+du,$$
and its spatially expanded coefficients
$$\widetilde b_j=\sum_iD_ia_{ij}+b_j+c_j,\qquad \widetilde c=\sum_iD_ib_i+d.$$
Assume $a,b$ have the pointwise spatial derivatives needed for the expanded coefficients, $a=a^T\ge\lambda_0I$ with $\lambda_0>0$, and every spatial boundary point has an exterior tangent ball. The classical equation is understood through these expanded nondivergence coefficients. Assume $a,\widetilde b,\widetilde c,f$ have finite source order-zero weighted parabolic Hölder norms and the additional source weighted bounds $|\delta\widetilde b|_\alpha,|\delta^2\widetilde c|_\alpha,|\delta^2f|_\alpha<\infty$. Here the order-zero convention is
$$|v|_{0,\alpha}=\sup_{P\in Q}|v(P)|+\sup_{P\ne R\in Q}\delta_{P,R}^{\alpha}\frac{|v(P)-v(R)|}{d_p(P,R)^\alpha},\qquad d_p(P,R)=(|x-y|^2+|t-s|)^{1/2},$$
with $\delta(P)=\min\{\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial U),\sqrt t\}$ and $\delta_{P,R}=\min\{\delta(P),\delta(R)\}$. Assume the initial datum $g$ and lateral datum $\varphi$ are Hölder continuous with compatible values $g(x)=\varphi(x,0)$ on $\partial U$. Retain the source barrier assumption that some $\theta>0$ satisfies $\theta^2a_{11}+\theta\widetilde b_1\ge1$ and its coefficient bounds
$$\sum_{i,j}|a_{ij}|^2\le\Lambda,\qquad \lambda_0^{-2}(|b|^2+|c|^2)+\lambda_0^{-1}|d|\le v^2.$$
Then the problem $-u_t+L_tu=f$, $u=g$ initially and $u=\varphi$ laterally has a unique solution
$$u^*\in C^{2+\alpha,1+\alpha/2}_{\mathrm{loc}}(U\times(0,T])\cap C(\bar U\times[0,T]).$$
Write $\psi$ for the combined prescribed datum and $\Gamma_T=(\bar U\times\{0\})\cup(\partial U\times[0,T])$. If $\widetilde c\le0$, every $h\in C^{2,1}(Q)\cap C(\bar U\times[0,T])$ with finite residual norm satisfies
$$\|h-u^*\|_\infty\le\|h-\psi\|_{C(\Gamma_T)}+T\|f+h_t-L_th\|_\infty.$$
Consequently any sequence whose two right-hand errors tend to zero converges uniformly to $u^*$. If it exactly satisfies the initial and lateral conditions, its residuals are also locally parabolic Hölder, and the displayed divergence-to-nondivergence expansion agrees in distributions locally, it converges strongly in $L^2(0,T;H^1(U))$. In particular these deterministic implications apply on every probability-one event where a PINN residual-consistency theorem supplies the stated residual and prescribed-data limits.
thm-neural-operator-discretization-invar:
## Statement

Let a finite neural operator have bounded domains, continuous kernels and biases, continuous pointwise activations, and continuous pointwise lifting and projection networks. For every integral use finite measurable partitions whose cells have tags, volume weights, and maximal diameter tending to zero. Its compatible quadratures converge in the output supremum norm uniformly on every compact input set in $C(\bar D)$, and hence on compact subsets of any Banach input space continuously included in $C(\bar D)$. Intermediate values in these realizations are evaluated by their defining functions at all required tags and output queries; changing meshes does not change the continuum parameters.

More generally, the same conclusion holds in the output Banach norm for the following compatible-space architecture. At each stage choose a Banach function space $X_t$ continuously included in $C(\bar D_t;\mathbb R^{q_t})$. For an integral layer from $X_t$ to an auxiliary Banach function space $Y_t$ of $\mathbb R^{q_{t+1}}$-valued functions on $\bar D_{t+1}$, require a continuous inclusion $Y_t\hookrightarrow C(\bar D_{t+1};\mathbb R^{q_{t+1}})$ and require that $y\mapsto\kappa_t(\cdot,y)$ be continuous from $\bar D_t$ into the space of linear maps $\mathbb R^{q_t}\to Y_t$, in operator norm. Every local linear term is a bounded map $X_t\to Y_t$, its bias belongs to $Y_t$, and its following activation is a continuous map $Y_t\to X_{t+1}$. Any separate lifting and projection maps are continuous between their specified Banach spaces. The same maps are used in the discrete and continuum constructions. No arbitrary output Banach norm follows from its continuous inclusion into the supremum norm alone.
lem-pinn-cell-occupancy-controls-uniform:
## Statement

Let $X\subset\mathbb R^D$ carry a probability measure $\mu$, let $s,c>0$, and fix an integer $m\ge1$. Put $\ell=(c\sqrt m)^{-1/s}$. Suppose a specified finite measurable partition $X_1,\ldots,X_K$ of $X$ has each cell contained in a cube of side $\ell$ and of mass at least $c\ell^s$. Let $Y_1,\ldots,Y_m$ be independent points of law $\mu$, and put $\delta=\sqrt D\ell$. With probability at least $\max\{0,1-\sqrt m\exp(-\sqrt m/8)\}$ every cell contains at least $\sqrt m/2$ samples, counted with multiplicity. On this event, simultaneously for all real functions $v,g$ with finite $\alpha$-Hölder seminorms on $X$,
$$\|v-g\|_{\infty;X}^2\le6\sqrt m\left(\frac1m\sum_{i=1}^m|v(Y_i)-g(Y_i)|^2\right)+3\delta^{2\alpha}([v]_{\alpha;X}^2+[g]_{\alpha;X}^2).$$
No independence between the functions and the samples is required.
thm-pinn-regularized-loss-consistency:
## Statement

Let $D\ge2$, $0<\alpha\le1$, and let the residual and boundary sets $U,\Gamma\subset\mathbb R^D$ carry probability measures $\mu_r,\mu_b$. Put $s_r=D$ and $s_b=D-1$. For $i=r,b$, fix $c_i,C_i,\ell_{0,i},\rho_{0,i}>0$ and a specified family of finite measurable partitions of the corresponding set at every $0<\ell\le\ell_{0,i}$. Each cell is contained in an ambient cube of side $\ell$ and has mass at least $c_i\ell^{s_i}$. Assume $\mu_i(\overline B_\rho(x))\le C_i\rho^{s_i}$ for centers in that set and $0<\rho\le\rho_{0,i}$. These are small-scale conditions. The usual Lipschitz-domain and positive-density hypotheses may be retained, but the explicit partition and ball bounds are the properties used below.

Take nested iid sample sequences of respective laws $\mu_r,\mu_b$ and counts $m_r,m_b\to\infty$. For sufficiently large counts put
$$\ell_i=(c_i\sqrt{m_i})^{-1/s_i},\qquad \delta_i=\sqrt D\ell_i,\qquad A_i=m_i^{-\alpha/s_i},$$
$$C_m=3\max_{i=r,b}\{(C_i/c_i)D^{s_i/2}\sqrt{m_i}\},\qquad \widehat\lambda^R_{i,m}=3\lambda_i\delta_i^{2\alpha}/C_m,$$
where $\lambda_r,\lambda_b>0$ are fixed. The count threshold is explicitly $m_i\ge\max\{1,c_i^{-2}\ell_{0,i}^{-2s_i},c_i^{-2}D^{s_i}\rho_{0,i}^{-2s_i}\}$; thus both partition and ball bounds apply. Choose weights $\lambda^R_{i,m}\ge\widehat\lambda^R_{i,m}$ and $\|\lambda_m^R\|_\infty=O(\|\widehat\lambda_m^R\|_\infty)$, with the same constants throughout the formulas.

Let $f,g$ have finite $\alpha$-Hölder seminorms on their respective sets. Let $H_m$ be trial classes for which $L[h]$ and $B[h]$ have finite such seminorms; in the PDE application retain $H_m\subset C^{k,\alpha}(U)\cap C^{0,\alpha}(\bar U)$. Suppose there are witnesses $u_m^*\in H_m$ with zero empirical PINN loss and $[L[u_m^*]]_{\alpha;U}^2+[B[u_m^*]]_{\alpha;\Gamma}^2\le M<\infty$, uniformly in $m$. Every global minimizer $h_m$ of the prescribed regularized empirical objective satisfies the following, uniformly for every such minimizer on the same sampling events.

On the hit-cell event, with probability at least $1-q(m_r)-q(m_b)$ (clipped at zero),
$$\operatorname{Loss}^{\mathrm{PINN}}(h_m;\lambda)=O(A_r+A_b),\qquad q(n)=\sqrt n(1-1/\sqrt n)^n.$$
If the residual and boundary sample streams are independent, the lower bound improves to $(1-q(m_r))(1-q(m_b))$, exactly the Appendix B probability. If the chosen $c_r,c_b\le1$, this also implies the weaker later printed bound with $1-c_i/\sqrt{m_i}$ in place of $1-1/\sqrt{m_i}$. No normalization is implicit.

On the occupancy event, with probability at least $1-Q(m_r)-Q(m_b)$ (clipped at zero),
$$\|L[h_m]-f\|_{\infty;U}^2+\|B[h_m]-g\|_{\infty;\Gamma}^2=O(A_r+A_b),\qquad Q(n)=\sqrt n e^{-\sqrt n/8}.$$
For independent streams one may instead use $\max\{0,1-Q(m_r)\}\max\{0,1-Q(m_b)\}$. Almost surely the two uniform errors tend to zero along any count pairs tending to infinity. If $m_r=O(m_b^{D/(D-1)})$, both displayed right sides are $O(m_r^{-\alpha/D})$. No comparability of the regularization coordinates is required. Constants in these bounds depend on $M$, the fixed data, and the constant in the weight upper bound. If the witness bound is almost surely finite rather than deterministic, the eventual almost-sure assertions hold with that random finite constant. These are statements about global minimizers, not a training algorithm.
lem-shin-smooth-dirichlet-approximants-f:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let all coefficients and data be real. Let $n\ge2$, and let $V\subset\mathbb R^n$ be nonempty and bounded with smooth boundary. Suppose $A,\beta,c,F,G$ are smooth on a neighborhood of $\bar V$, $A=A^T$, $\lambda I\le A\le\Lambda I$ for constants $0<\lambda\le\Lambda$, and $c\le0$. For $L=A:D^2+\beta\cdot D+c$, the Dirichlet problem $Lu=F$ in $V$, $u=G$ on $\partial V$ has exactly one solution $u\in C^\infty(\bar V)$. Here smoothness on the closure means that all interior derivatives extend continuously to the closure, equivalently that a smooth extension exists to every finite differentiability order.
lem-shin-uniform-boundary-schauder-estim:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Fix $n\ge2$ and $0<\alpha<1$. Consider a family of bounded smooth domains $V$ in a fixed bounded set with a common finite boundary graph atlas: the graph radii, inverse-chart radii and bounds for all chart and inverse-chart derivatives through order two and the $\alpha$-Hölder seminorms of their second derivatives are uniformly controlled. Let $L=A:D^2+\beta\cdot D+c$ have real smooth coefficients near $\bar V$, with $A=A^T$, $\lambda I\le A\le\Lambda I$ for fixed $0<\lambda\le\Lambda$, and uniformly bounded global $C^{0,\alpha}(\bar V)$ coefficient norms. There is a uniform $C<\infty$ such that every real $u\in C^\infty(\bar V)$ with zero boundary values satisfies
$$\|u\|_{C^{2,\alpha}(\bar V)}\le C\bigl(\|u\|_{\infty;V}+\|Lu\|_{C^{0,\alpha}(\bar V)}\bigr).$$
The constant depends only on the stated uniform geometric and coefficient controls, dimension and exponent, and not on higher smoothness norms. No sign of $c$ is required for this a priori estimate.

Furthermore every nonempty bounded $C^{2,\alpha}$ domain $U\subset\mathbb R^n$ has smooth bounded open subsets $V_j$ with $\bar V_j\subset U$, every compact subset of $U$ eventually contained in $V_j$, and a common finite graph atlas with the uniform controls just described. Nestedness is not asserted or required.
thm-shin-elliptic-dirichlet-existence-an:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let all coefficients and data be real. Let $n\ge1$, $0<\alpha<1$, and let $U\subset\mathbb R^n$ be nonempty, bounded and Lipschitz, with an exterior ball at every boundary point. Suppose $a_{ij}=a_{ji},b_i\in C^{1,\alpha}(U)$ and $c_i,d\in C^{0,\alpha}(U)$, with finite global norms, and $\lambda_0 I\le A=(a_{ij})\le\Lambda_0 I$ for constants $0<\lambda_0\le\Lambda_0$. Define
$$L[u]=\sum_{i,j}D_i(a_{ij}D_ju)+\sum_iD_i(b_i u)+\sum_i c_iD_iu+du,$$
$$\beta_j=\sum_iD_ia_{ij}+b_j+c_j,\qquad \gamma=\sum_iD_ib_i+d,$$
and assume $\gamma\le0$. Retain, when required by the source application, the bounds $\sum_{i,j}|a_{ij}|^2\le\Lambda$ and $\lambda_0^{-2}(|b|^2+|c|^2)+\lambda_0^{-1}|d|\le v^2$.

For every $f\in C^{0,\alpha}(U)$ and $g\in C(\partial U)$ there is exactly one solution
$$u\in C^{2,\alpha}_{\mathrm{loc}}(U)\cap C(\bar U),\qquad Lu=f,\qquad u|_{\partial U}=g.$$
There is a finite constant $C_L$, depending on $U$, ellipticity and the sup bounds of the expanded coefficients $A,\beta,\gamma$, such that every $h\in C^2(U)\cap C(\bar U)$ with bounded residual satisfies
$$\|u-h\|_{\infty;U}\le C_L\bigl(\|f-Lh\|_{\infty;U}+\|g-h\|_{\infty;\partial U}\bigr).$$
If $g=0$, then $u\in H^1_0(U)$ and $\|u\|_{H^1(U)}\le C_E\|f\|_{\infty;U}$, where $C_E$ may additionally depend on $\|DA\|_\infty$. If $g$ is the restriction of an ambient $C^{2,\alpha}$ lifting $G$ near $\bar U$, then $u-G\in H^1_0(U)$. If in addition $U$ is $C^{2,\alpha}$ and $g$ has such a lifting $G$, the solution lies in $C^{2,\alpha}(\bar U)$ and satisfies
$$\|u\|_{2,\alpha;\bar U}\le C\bigl(\|f\|_{0,\alpha;U}+\|G\|_{2,\alpha;\bar U}\bigr).$$
The global branch follows by uniform estimates on smooth interior approximants and passage to the classical limit.
thm-pinn-linear-elliptic-consistency:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Use the corrected small-scale sampling, trial-class, exact-zero-witness, and exact regularization hypotheses of the regularized PINN theorem, with residual and boundary operators $L$ and boundary restriction. Let $d\ge2$ and let $U\subset\mathbb R^d$ be bounded Lipschitz with an exterior sphere at every boundary point. For $0<\alpha<1$, let $a_{ij}=a_{ji}\in C^{1,\alpha}(U)$ have minimum eigenvalue at least $\lambda_0>0$, let $b_i\in C^{1,\alpha}(U)$ and $c_i,d\in C^{0,\alpha}(U)$, and put
$$L[u]=\sum_{i,j}D_i(a_{ij}D_j u)+\sum_iD_i(b_i u)+\sum_i c_iD_i u+du,$$
$$\widetilde b_j=\sum_iD_i a_{ij}+b_j+c_j,\qquad \widetilde c=\sum_iD_i b_i+d\le0.$$
All indicated Hölder norms are finite global norms. Retain the source coefficient bounds $\sum_{i,j}|a_{ij}|^2\le\Lambda$ and $\lambda_0^{-2}(|b|^2+|c|^2)+\lambda_0^{-1}|d|\le v^2$. Let $f\in C^{0,\alpha}(U)$ and $g\in C^{0,\alpha}(\partial U)$. There is exactly one $u^*\in C^{2,\alpha}_{\mathrm{loc}}(U)\cap C^0(\bar U)$ with $L[u^*]=f$ and $u^*=g$ on $\partial U$.

Every sequence of global regularized empirical minimizers $h_m$ converges to $u^*$ in $C^0(U)$ almost surely as both sample counts tend to infinity. If $m_r=O(m_b^{d/(d-1)})$, the occupancy-event squared uniform error is $O(m_r^{-\alpha/d})$, with the probability and constants of the regularized-loss theorem. If each minimizer satisfies the boundary data exactly, the errors belong to $H^1_0(U)$ and converge to zero in $H^1(U)$ almost surely. If in addition $U$ is $C^{2,\alpha}$ and $g$ has a $C^{2,\alpha}$ lifting, the usual global $C^{2,\alpha}(\bar U)$ branch applies with its stated coefficient/data hypotheses. No global Hölder regularity is claimed from the exterior-sphere condition alone, and no optimizer convergence is asserted.
thm-pinn-linear-parabolic-consistency:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $U\subset\mathbb R^d$ be bounded with an exterior ball at every spatial boundary point, $T>0$, and $Q=U\times(0,T)$. Use the full parabolic coefficient/data hypotheses of the variable-coefficient existence theorem: differentiability of $a_{ij},b_i$, symmetry and uniform ellipticity, the source weighted parabolic Hölder coefficient bounds, bounded locally parabolic Hölder expanded drift and potential, bounded locally parabolic Hölder forcing, compatible Hölder initial and lateral data, and one-sided local Hölder control at interior points of the final face. Use
$$L_t[u]=\sum_{i,j}D_i(a_{ij}D_j u)+\sum_iD_i(b_i u)+\sum_i c_iD_i u+du,$$
$$\widetilde b_i=\sum_jD_j a_{ij}+b_i+c_i,\qquad\widetilde c=\sum_iD_i b_i+d\le0.$$
Retain the source pointwise bounds with constants $\lambda_0,\Lambda,v$ and its auxiliary $\theta>0$ condition $\theta^2a_{11}+\theta\widetilde b_1\ge1$; the direct parabolic time barrier also works without that auxiliary condition. Boundedness is part of the source's order-zero Hölder norm, not a consequence of its weighted $\delta^2f$ bound alone.

Use the corrected small-scale sampling, data/trial-class, exact-zero-witness and exact regularization assumptions of the regularized PINN theorem in the ambient dimension $D=d+1$, with residual $-h_t+L_t[h]$, target $f$, and restriction to the initial-lateral boundary $\Gamma_T$ with target $\psi$ combining the compatible data. The Euclidean Hölder assumptions in this sampling interface are retained in addition to the parabolic PDE regularity assumptions. There is one classical solution $u^*\in C^{2,1}(Q)\cap C(\bar U\times[0,T])$, locally parabolic Hölder in its displayed derivatives, to $-u_t^*+L_t[u^*]=f$ and the prescribed data.

Every sequence of global empirical regularized minimizers converges to $u^*$ in $C^0(Q)$ almost surely as both counts tend to infinity. For $m_r=O(m_b^{(d+1)/d})$, the occupancy-event squared uniform solution error is $O(m_r^{-\alpha/(d+1)})$, with the probability and constants of the regularized-loss theorem at dimension $D=d+1$. If all minimizers satisfy both initial and lateral data exactly and the displayed divergence expansion agrees distributionally with the classical operator (in particular if $a,b$ are spatially $C^1$ locally), then their errors belong to $L^2(0,T;H^1_0(U))$ and tend to zero in $L^2(0,T;H^1(U))$ almost surely. The energy conclusion uses the actual bounded divergence coefficients and their source $v$ bound. No closed-cylinder $C^{2,1}$ regularity of $u^*$ or convergence of an optimizer is asserted.
thm-neural-operator-compact-uniform-univ:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ and $D'\subset\mathbb R^{d'}$ be bounded Lipschitz domains. Let $A$ be $L^{p_1}(D)$, $W^{m_1,p_1}(D)$, or $C(\bar D)$, with $1\le p_1<\infty$ and $m_1\ge1$ where applicable. Let $U$ be $L^{p_2}(D')$, $W^{m_2,p_2}(D')$, or $C^{m_2}(\bar D')$, with $1\le p_2<\infty$, with $m_2=0$ in the Lebesgue case, $m_2\ge1$ in the Sobolev case, and $m_2\ge0$ in the continuous case. Let $G^\dagger:A\to U$ be continuous, $K\subset A$ compact, and $\varepsilon>0$. Suppose $\sigma_1\in\mathcal A_0^L$, $\sigma_2\in\mathcal A_0$, and $\sigma_3\in\mathcal A_{m_2}$ in every finite input dimension used below. Then some finite-layer neural operator $G$ in the specified integral architecture satisfies
$$\sup_{a\in K}\|G^\dagger(a)-G(a)\|_U<\varepsilon.$$

The printed additional source implication asserts that, if $U$ is Hilbert, $M>0$, $\|G^\dagger(a)\|_U\le M$ on all $A$, and $\sigma_1\in\mathrm{BA}$, then $\|G(a)\|_U\le4M$ on all $A$. This exact implication is vacuous because its diameter-bounded class is empty. A useful corrected implication replaces only that additional activation premise by the following explicitly different property: for every compact $S\subset\mathbb R^q$, every $C\ge\sup_{z\in S}|z|_2$ with the convention that the radius of the empty set is zero, and every $\eta>0$, there is a $\sigma_1$ MLP $b:\mathbb R^q\to\mathbb R^q$ with $\sup_S|b(z)-z|_2<\eta$ and $\sup_{\mathbb R^q}|b(z)|_2\le C$. Under this replacement the same global bound $4M$ holds. This replacement does not change the printed diameter-based definition.
lem-ap-finite-dimensional-factorization-:
## Statement

Let $X,Y$ be real Banach spaces with the approximation property, $T:X\to Y$ continuous, $K\subset X$ compact, and $\varepsilon>0$. There are integers $J,s\ge1$, bounded linear maps $E:X\to\mathbb R^J$ and $B:\mathbb R^s\to Y$, and continuous $h:\mathbb R^J\to\mathbb R^s$ such that $\sup_{x\in K}\|T(x)-Bh(E(x))\|_Y<\varepsilon$. In particular $E(x)=(\ell_j(x))_{j=1}^J$ for bounded linear functionals $\ell_j$, and $Bv=\sum_{i=1}^s v_i\beta_i$ for finitely many $\beta_i\in Y$.
lem-inward-mollification-and-finite-rank:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded Lipschitz open set, with $d\ge1$, and let $m\in\mathbb N_0$. Let $X$ be either $W^{m,p}(D;\mathbb R)$ for $1\le p<\infty$, including $W^{0,p}(D)=L^p(D)$, or $C^m(\bar D;\mathbb R)$. In the latter space derivatives in $D$ extend continuously to $\bar D$, and the norm is $\max_{|\alpha|\le m}\sup_{\bar D}|D^\alpha u|$. For every norm-compact $K\subseteq X$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, there is a bounded finite-rank linear map $F:X\to X$ such that $\sup_{u\in K}\|Fu-u\|_X<\varepsilon$ and whose range is contained in the restrictions to $D$ of functions in $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$, with their continuous boundary values in the $C^m$ case. In particular, such smooth restrictions are norm-dense in $X$.

Moreover, there are finitely many ambient smooth cutoffs $\psi_j$, vectors $v_j$, a unit-mass $\rho\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$, and $t_0>0$ such that for $0<t<t_0$ the kernel $k_t(x,y)=\sum_j\psi_j(x)\rho_t(x+tv_j-y)$, with $\rho_t(z)=t^{-d}\rho(z/t)$, defines bounded linear smoothing maps $S_tu(x)=\int_Dk_t(x,y)u(y)\,dy$. They satisfy $\sup_{0<t<t_0}\|S_t\|_{X\to X}<\infty$ and $\sup_{u\in K}\|S_tu-u\|_X\to0$ for every norm-compact $K\subset X$. Each kernel is ambient smooth with fixed compact support in its first variable.
lem-smooth-integral-functionals-approxim:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain, and let $X=L^p(D)$, $X=W^{m,p}(D)$, or $X=C^m(\bar D)$, where $1\le p<\infty$ and $m\ge0$ wherever applicable. For every bounded linear functional $L:X\to\mathbb R$, every compact $K\subset X$, and every $\varepsilon>0$, there is $\kappa\in C_c^\infty(D)$ such that
$$\sup_{a\in K}\left|L(a)-\int_D\kappa(y)a(y)\,dy\right|<\varepsilon.$$

The input function in this integral is its zeroth derivative. The conclusion is compact-uniform, without an assertion of operator-norm density of these functionals.
